A1.justification: Both PDFs present the same MANU study with complete, readable text, equations, eight tables, twelve figures, and Appendices A–E. Text and rendered-page comparisons establish reliable alignment without material gaps.

before.justification: v2 reports original MANU experiments on LLaVA and Idefics2, including unlearning and utility results, importance-function ablations, and larger-model evaluation (Tables 1, 4, 7, and 8).

after.justification: v3 retains original experimental outcomes on LLaVA and Idefics2 in the main text and Appendix E, including utility evaluations, ablations, and LLaVA-13B results.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same four neuron-importance functions, forget/retain scoring ratio, neuron selection, and weight-zeroing procedure. No method component changes.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same MLLMU-Bench tasks and multimodal/text-only scenarios, plus MMMU, LLaVA-Bench, MIA-Bench, MM-Vet, and MMStar. Appendix coverage is unchanged.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is identical within corresponding experiments. GA, Gradient Difference, KL Minimization, NPO, Prompting, and reference models retain their original participation, including the appendix comparisons.

E3.justification: The forget splits, evaluated model sizes, data transformations, evaluation metrics, and testing procedures in Section 4 and Appendices B–E are unchanged.

E4.justification: Both retain the same pruning-ratio studies (Tables 2 and 5), importance-function ablations (Table 7), activation and modality analyses, utility trade-off analyses, and illustrative cases.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Uncertainty-reporting practices are unchanged.

E6.justification: Numerical entries, plotted results, and qualitative findings are unchanged throughout both PDFs. For example, Table 1 retains MANU's 38.36% forget and 44.89% retain classification accuracy for LLaVA-1.5-7B with 10% forget data.

T1.justification: The importance-function definitions, scoring and pruning formulas, and baseline-loss equations in Section 3 and Appendix D are identical. No formal assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain identical claims about modality-aware pruning, balanced unlearning across modalities, and preservation of model utility.

C2.justification: Interpretations of modality imbalance and pruning/utility trade-offs are unchanged. Section 8 preserves the same limitations concerning fictitious profiles, unexplored applications, attack robustness, and instability.

D1.justification: Section 4.3 and Appendix D retain the same hardware, batch size, NPO hyperparameter, and implementation information. The code-access link is unchanged; the added funding acknowledgment supplies no technical or reproducibility details.

R1.justification: The cited works, bibliography entries, and research positioning are identical. References reflow across pages without additions or removals.

P1.justification: v3 adds Section 9, Acknowledgment, identifying NSF and ONR funding, and updates the arXiv version/date stamp. The research prose and appendix organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The acknowledgment causes limited reference-list reflow across PDF pages 9–12. All twelve figures and eight tables retain their content, formatting, and placement.

improvement.justification: v3 makes funding attribution explicit, but the scientific arguments, empirical evidence, technical documentation, and limitations are identical, including the appendices. The acknowledgment and minor reference reflow do not materially change overall paper quality.
